name: owner_control_decision_v1
description: Canonical owner-control decision, bound to owner_control_manifest_v1 by id, digest, audience and nonce, exactly as a task decision binds to its manifest. What differs is the domain, the signing context, and the key role: only the owner-control signer may carry it, and its covered bytes are prefixed with the owner-control tag. A decision is evidence, never authority. signing_context_tag is the domain separation tag for this object's domain. signing_preimage_hex is tag || 0x00 || canonical_json bytes, and signing_preimage_sha256_hex is its SHA-256. This is the byte range a signer would cover. Nothing in this repository signs or verifies; only the preimage is defined. The tag is NOT a field of the object: a verifier derives it from the object type it is verifying, so a caller cannot supply or substitute it. That is what makes the two domains cryptographically distinct rather than merely distinguishable: a signature over a task-approval object cannot be a valid signature over an owner-control object even if every field were manipulated to match, because the covered bytes differ in a prefix neither party controls.
